title: How Women Rise: Break the 12 Habits Holding You Back from Your Next Raise, Promotion, or Job
author: Sally Helgesen
Marshall Goldsmith
target_audience: Women aspiring to leadership or executive roles
Managers, HR professionals, and executives seeking to support female talent
Anyone interested in gender dynamics in the workplace
core_themes: Unique barriers women face in career advancement
primary_purpose: To identify the key habits that often hold women back from professional advancement, and to offer practical advice for breaking these habits and achieving greater success in their careers.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, encouraging, research-based with anecdotes and real-life examples
structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic sections focusing on each of the 12 habits, building context and solutions for each
features: Case studies and stories from professional women
Summaries and actionable steps at the end of each habit

key_concepts_lessons: Women often succeed early in their careers by adopting certain habits, but these same habits can become obstacles as they rise.
Awareness is the first step: identifying and understanding the 12 self-limiting habits.

Common unhelpful habits include reluctance to claim achievements, expecting others to notice and reward hard work, overvaluing expertise, building rather than leveraging relationships, and failing to enlist allies.
Practical strategies, such as learning to self-promote, broaden networks, and articulate ambitions, are essential for advancement.
Changing habits requires conscious effort, support, and sometimes mentorship or coaching.
Effective leadership growth for women involves both overcoming internal barriers and navigating external workplace dynamics.
notable_features: Focuses on habits particularly prevalent among professional women
Co-authored by leading experts in women’s leadership and executive coaching
cultural_historical_context: Published at a time of increased attention to gender equity in the workplace, on the heels of the #MeToo movement and global conversations about women’s leadership, the book addresses both contemporary and persistent barriers faced by women at work.
reception_impact: Well-received by business leaders and gender equity advocates
Frequently recommended for women’s leadership programs and workplace trainings
Praised for being both insightful and deeply actionable
Has sparked workshops, talks, and further research into women’s career advancement
comparable_titles: Lean In: Women, Work, and the Will to Lead by Sheryl Sandberg
The Confidence Code: The Science and Art of Self-Assurance—What Women Should Know by Katty Kay and Claire Shipman
